messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Upgrade playbook launch & schedule QBR

Hi Alex —

Following our renewal conversation last week, we put together an initial upgrade playbook that outlines two paths we typically see: a capacity-first uplift (short-term burst + reserved capacity) and a staged-term uplift (stair-step commits with exec checkpoints). I attached the one-page playbook to this email (redwood-upgrade-playbook-v1.pdf).

Can you confirm the business driver for this cycle (throughput vs. cost predictability vs. feature access)? That'll help us recommend the right path. Also looking to lock a 60-minute QBR to align execs + SREs next week so we can finalize the MAP and pricing. Proposed slots:
- Thu 12/17 10:00–11:00 AM PST
- Fri 12/18 2:00–3:00 PM PST

Favored next steps:
1) Quick QBR (60m) to align stakeholders and finalize capacity numbers
2) Draft mutual action plan (MAP) and term amendment for review
3) Legal procurement check (if price or term changes require redline)

I've CC'd Stephanie (CSM) and Marissa (Solutions) to join the QBR — Stephanie will run the agenda, Marissa can walk technical sizing.

Attachments: redwood-upgrade-playbook-v1.pdf

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0143
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@cloudforge.com>

Cc: Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@cloudforge.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Upgrade playbook launch & schedule QBR

Ben —

Thanks for the deck. CloudForge is definitely moving to a higher throughput commitment in Q1; our infra spike around product search has us looking at a ~2.5x committed token baseline for peak windows. Cost predictability is important but the main ask is headroom for burst capacity during major crawl/index events.

Both proposed slots work for me, lean toward Thu 12/17 at 10:00 AM PST. Can you send a short exec summary for my CFO and our Head of Ops — one slide that shows delta in cost and latency per option? Also want to confirm whether the staged-term model affects invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudForge
alex.johnson@cloudforge.com
